draft.title: From republic to empire
card: Republic
Rome was a republic for about 500 years. Two consuls were elected each year to lead, and the Senate, a council of powerful men, advised them and made the big decisions.
Civil wars

In the 1st century BCE, powerful generals fought each other in civil wars, which are wars between people of the same state. Julius Caesar won one of these wars and became dictator, a ruler with almost total power.
Caesar's end
In 44 BCE, a group of senators killed Caesar. They said they wanted to protect the republic, but more civil wars followed.
Empire
Caesar's adopted son Octavian won the last of these wars. In 27 BCE he took the name Augustus and became the first emperor, and Rome became an empire ruled by one person.
draft.remember: Rome moved from elected leaders and the Senate to rule by one emperor after years of civil war.

a.q: How was Rome governed before it had emperors?
opts: By elected consuls and the Senate
By one emperor chosen by the army
By a dictator who ruled for life
By kings from one family
a.why: In the republic, two consuls were elected each year and the Senate advised them and made decisions. Rule by one person came later, when Augustus became emperor. A dictator such as Caesar held power only at the end of the republic.
a.clue: Think about who led Rome for about 500 years before Augustus.

b.q: Why did Rome stop being a republic and become an empire?
opts: Civil wars ended with Augustus taking sole power
Caesar's killers created the empire as they planned
Voters chose Augustus to be emperor in an election
Foreign armies conquered the Senate and took over
b.why: Years of civil wars between powerful men ended when Octavian won and became Augustus, the first emperor. Caesar's killers said they wanted to save the republic, so the empire was not their plan, even though their act led to more wars.
b.clue: Look at what Octavian did after the last civil war.

a.best: By elected consuls and the Senate

b.best: Civil wars ended with Augustus taking sole power

problems.detail: 'Before it had emperors' also covers the time of the kings, who ruled before the republic, and Caesar's brief life dictatorship. 'By kings from one family' and 'By a dictator who ruled for life' then look partly defensible. Ask 'How was Rome governed during the republic?' instead.
